history.origins: Diloti originated in Greece and is a cornerstone of Greek coffee-shop (kafeneio) gaming culture. It evolved by merging older fishing games (Kontsina) with matching bonuses (Xeri) and strategic declarations.
timeline: Early 20th Century: Developed as a competitive alternative to simpler fishing games.
1950s-Present: Established as a major social game across Greece and Cyprus.
Modern Era: Widely played online and in tournaments.
history.cultural: In Greece, Diloti is considered a game of high skill and memory, often compared to bridge in terms of the partnership awareness required.
history.evolution: The game's name identifies the 'declaration' phase as its unique selling point, separating it from the purely reactive nature of older fishing games.

setup.deck: 52 cards. Aces rank as 1 for sums, but otherwise have high point value.
setup.dealing: 6 cards per player; 4 face-up on table. If 3 or 4 face cards of same value are on the table, it's a misdeal.

rules.objective: Score points by capturing key cards, winning most cards, and making xeri sweeps; first to 61 points usually wins.
rules.gameplay:
1. Fishing: Match a card from hand to one on the table (for number cards you may also capture a chosen sum-equal combination).
2. Face Cards: J/Q/K capture exactly one matching face card and cannot be used in sum captures or declarations.
3. Declarations (Builds): Create plain or group declarations from number cards. A player making or raising a declaration must hold a matching card for later capture.
4. Raising and ownership: Opponents may raise plain declarations; group declarations cannot be raised. The player who most recently created/added to a declaration is responsible for capturing it.
5. Xeri: Capturing all table cards in one play scores 10 points (with standard exceptions for the opening table-clear and some end-of-round cases).
6. Further deals: When hands are exhausted, dealer gives 6 new cards each from stock; no new table cards are dealt.
keyRules: Must follow suit is NOT applicable (Fishing game).
Face cards cannot be part of sum-captures.
A successful Xeri is marked by placing a card face-up under the capture pile.
Aces are worth 1 point each and count as 1 in numerical captures.
In 4-player games, declarations bind only the player who made them, not the partner.

strategy.basic: Prioritize capturing the 10 of Diamonds and the 2 of Clubs.
strategy.intermediate: Use declarations to trap opponent cards. If you see an opponent building a 10, try to raise it to an 11 if you have one.
strategy.advanced: Memory-based clearing: Track which Kings and Queens have been played to set up a mid-game Xeri when you hold the final matching card.
tips: Don't leave a single low card on the table if the opponent can Xeri it.
The 'Most Cards' bonus (4 points) is often the deciding factor in close games.
Declarations are your best defense against having your table cards stolen.

scoring.description: Points come from most cards, aces, 10 of diamonds, 2 of clubs, and xeri sweeps.
scoring.winCondition: First side or player to reach 61 points wins.
